Messages.Author: ste...@sympatico.ca
Messages.Body:
The situation is this: Player A attempts to call a vote. player B has a
minion with a Blessing. If the minion with a Blessing attempts to block
player A can't play any cards requiring Presence. What determines an attempt
to block? If the minion with Blessing doesn't even have 1 intercept to block
can he still declare an attempted block that fails just so player A cannot
play any Presence cards during the vote?

Does Reform body require the reacting vampire being burnt to be in combat?
If so, what about after Nakova's ability happens?

Thanks,
Dave Stevers

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
ste...@sympatico.ca wrote:
>
> The situation is this: Player A attempts to call a vote. player B has a
> minion with a Blessing. If the minion with a Blessing attempts to block
> player A can't play any cards requiring Presence. What determines an attempt
> to block? If the minion with Blessing doesn't even have 1 intercept to block
> can he still declare an attempted block that fails just so player A cannot
> play any Presence cards during the vote?

Any attempt to block is an attempt to block, even if the minion making
the attempt never has enough intercept. Note that the minion chosen
must be capable of blocking (i.e., he cannot be the subject of an
Incriminating Video of the acting minion, the action must be blockable,
etc.).

> Does Reform body require the reacting vampire being burnt to be in combat?

Yes.

> If so, what about after Nakova's ability happens?

Sure. The 4 damage from Nakova's special occurs during combat.

Upon re-reading the question, it occurs that you may be asking about
reforming Nakova, which you can do. However, since this happens
"instead" of burning her, the opposing minion takes no damage from
Nakova's special.
